findings.title: Physical tap carrier identity replaces real emitted delimiter identity
findings.qualification: Authenticated executable AutoHotkey and shared catalogue control flow only; no AutoHotkey execution, native send, LED or receiving application tested.
findings.reproduction: Set idle0, all pointer kinds false, terminators=[tab], no AI tooltip/nav layer/modifiers. Configure tap_hold inherit_defaults=false and tab.tap_action=backspace without a hold; activate CapsWord independently, type two letters then press Tab. Its generic tap-only SC00F route deactivates before real Backspace despite no typed delimiter. Opposite control: terminators=[enter], caps_lock.tap_action=enter without hold: actual action emits Enter yet CapsWord survives. CapsWord native SC039/SC01C bindings do not intercept either carrier. Native sending/case/receiving unexecuted.
findings.root_cause: The automatic-end predicate asks physical KeyId before the real configured action runs. Physical tab falsely ends before configured Backspace; physical caps_lock misses configured Enter. Emitted SendLevel0 native keys are invisible to the I1 observer and their synthetic buffer effect never publishes a CapsWord delimiter to repair the decision.
findings.silent_failure: The chosen tap callback can run successfully, so no sender/configuration error is raised. Existing tap-unlatch regression passes only a marker callback and never emits a remapped action.
findings.regression_test: Exercise public Tab/CapsLock tap-only producers, real action resolver and state owner over passive send/LED ports. Compare native Tab, Tab->Backspace, CapsLock->Enter/Space, held modifiers, checked/unchecked delimiters and send refusal. Require automatic ending to follow qualifying acknowledged output. Qualify native Space HotIf priority independently; direct dispatcher calls cannot prove it.

findings.title: AltGr pre-clears CapsWord before its configured toggle so a second tap cannot switch it off
findings.qualification: Deduced from authenticated actual producer/action/state-owner statement order. No AutoHotkey execution or native AltGr receiving measured.
findings.reproduction: Set idle0, no terminators and every pointer kind false; configure AltGr tap caps_word with Shift hold. Two separate short isolated admitted AltGr taps first turn CapsWord on, then unconditionally disable and toggle it back on instead of turning it off. AltGr->Backspace with all automatic ends disabled demonstrates the same pre-clear as a sibling symptom.
findings.root_cause: _AltGrHandleHold calls DisableCapsWord unconditionally in the accepted isolated-tap branch, then AltGrTapHoldDispatchV2 resolves and runs the configured action. caps_word invokes ToggleCapsWord, which flips the freshly cleared Boolean, losing the prior toggle intent.
findings.silent_failure: Both individual state operations and the configured action succeed, leaving LED/state on; direct two-toggle state tests bypass the AltGr producer.
findings.regression_test: Drive real _AltGrHandleHold, action lookup and CapsWord state owner with recorded hold/send/LED boundaries. Require two admitted caps_word taps off->on->off; cover actual checked delimiter, Backspace, refused tap and pass-through guards/fake-LCtrl ownership.

findings.title: Changing the live idle delay can leave CapsWord without an expiry timer
findings.qualification: Actual menu renderer/callback, settings policy and watcher; recorded timer/eventtap/writer ports. All pointer auto-off kinds are disabled before activation so using the menu does not end the session. Persistence is an accepted save port, not a disk receipt. No native CapsLock receiving or elapsed-latency measurement.
findings.reproduction: Set every shortcuts.caps_word.pointer kind false and idle_timeout_seconds=0, activate CapsWord, choose the real menu 1-second preset, accept saving, type an ordinary letter, and advance controlled monotonic time more than 1 second after it. The real policy is now1000ms and the menu accepted, but no timer exists and no clear is requested. Alternatively start10seconds, choose1, type a letter, and cross the new idle deadline: the old10-second timer is the first chance to clear. Positive controls: a fresh1-second activation clears;1→0 suppresses the existing timer;1→10 reschedules; the next activation acquires1second; refused save restores0; delimiter checkbox changes act on the next key.
findings.root_cause: menu_caps_word.commit calls CapsWordAutoOff.apply_state, replacing the policy immediately. No timer owner is notified. start_capsword_idle_clock runs only on activation and note_capsword_activated; handle_capsword_event/output update the last-activity timestamp but never acquire a missing timer or reschedule an earlier deadline. An existing callback reads the new policy, producing asymmetric live behavior rather than a deliberate per-session snapshot.
findings.silent_failure: The menu applies/saves/refreshes successfully. Timer absence is not an error and no callback later diagnoses an active session lacking its newly selected deadline.
findings.regression_test: Drive actual menu callback with pointer exits disabled, an active session, and recorded native scheduler. Test0→1,10→1,1→0,1→10,1→0→1, successful/refused save, next typed key, activation and lifecycle teardown. Assert the chosen effective deadline is enforced without duplicate/stale timers; preserve deliberately different Windows next-activation policy.

findings.title: Inactive pointer traffic masks the first checked pointer event after activation
findings.qualification: Actual watcher, real serialized variable owner and real control-sentinel owner over recorded CLI/timer/eventtap/LED ports. Controlled timestamps establish ordering; no measured native timing or physical lock outcome.
findings.reproduction: With default pointer kinds enabled and idle0, send mouseMoved while CapsWord is inactive at1000s. Activate through the exact-token native control signal at1000.01s; send one checked click/gesture/scroll at1000.05s. CapsWord remains logically active, no CLI clear task exists, and no LED-off request occurs. Fresh activation without the earlier inactive pointer clears on that same click; a click at1000.1s clears; a typed delimiter at50ms bypasses the throttle.
findings.root_cause: deactivate_capsword updates _capsword_last_check_ns before asking supersede_capsword_activation whether any active intent exists. Activation does not reset that throttle. The shared100ms check is applied to all non-immediate pointer kinds, including discrete clicks and touch/gesture events, not only repeated motion.
findings.silent_failure: The early return neither logs nor retains the discrete event. A later physical pointer event or another terminator can clear it; that later success does not replay the lost event.
findings.regression_test: Exercise inactive pointer→activation→single checked discrete pointer inside100ms through actual control/event owners, every enabled/disabled pointer kind, exact threshold, continuous-motion coalescing and a fresh activation. Preserve cheap motion throttling while never borrowing a prior inactive session timestamp to discard a new session exit.

findings.title: A previous clear pending completion masks a fresh activation's delimiter
findings.qualification: Actual watcher plus real KeVariables/control-sentinel owners. The native-port fixture explicitly separates a published CLI payload from its pending process-exit callback, permitting the generated variable_unless activation path. The native ordering window is controlled, not physically reproduced.
findings.reproduction: Idle0 and a checked space. Activate CapsWord, let a pointer request an asynchronous clear, then publish that task's exact capsword0 payload while holding its completion callback. With the native variable now0, deliver a valid new activation1 control edge. Type a checked space while the previous clear completion is still pending. Logical activation remains1, no second clear is queued and no immediate LED-off is requested. Complete the old task without applying its already-published payload twice: revision guards correctly preserve the newer activation, but the space is never replayed. A later second space clears it.
findings.root_cause: _capsword_check_pending represents the previous asynchronous clear but is not reset/revision-scoped on a newly observed activation. deactivate_capsword returns at that flag even for an immediate typed delimiter. The old callback eventually releases the flag and discards its stale LED effect, but there is no retained latest deactivation intent to retry.
findings.silent_failure: The intended pending-operation suppression emits no refusal and retains no deferred delimiter intent. Old-writer completion reports successful settlement even though the newer activation's exit was dropped.
findings.regression_test: Split actual serialized writer publication and callback delivery, admit a newer exact-token activation only after publication0, then deliver a checked delimiter or accepted driver-output delimiter before old completion. Assert current-generation clear is retained/admitted and eventually enforced, with no stale LED reset, duplicate native writes, wrong-token publication or replay after teardown.

findings.title: Absolute pointer motion never reaches CapsWord pointer-motion auto-off
findings.reproduction: Before activation set shortcuts.caps_word.idle_timeout_seconds=0, pointer.gesture=false and pointer.pointer_motion=true. Use an accepted EV_ABS touchpad. Activate CapsWord; a BTN_TOUCH down is unchecked. Report initial ABS_X=100, ABS_Y=200, SYN_REPORT, then changed ABS_X=127, ABS_Y=212, SYN_REPORT. CapsWord and its capture lock remain active; the original Hook emits only press/frame notifications, no motion. A subsequent EV_REL/REL_X=1 on the relative-mouse control emits motion and ends/unlocks the same session.
findings.root_cause: adapters.keyboard_hook._dispatch_pointer publishes motion exclusively for InputEvent.EV_REL, while modules.hotstrings.device_finder accepts EV_ABS touchpads/tablets and the shared manifest declares pointer_motion supported. Main forwards only the events it receives; the missing absolute reports cannot reach the compiled policy.
findings.silent_failure: The pointer stream is readable and its SYN_REPORT callbacks continue normally; no missing-dispatch warning is logged. Default gesture=true can mask the missing motion route by ending the session on the initial touch, and existing pointer-policy tests call already-classified kinds.
findings.regression_test: Drive an accepted absolute pointer through the genuine reader/pump and original dispatch: establish prior ABS_X/Y, change one coordinate meaningfully, then SYN_REPORT. With gesture=false,pointer_motion=true,idle0, end and unlock exactly once; unchecked pointer_motion must retain the session. Keep relative-mouse and default-contact controls, and qualify native compositor receiving separately.
findings.qualification: Executed original Hook dispatch, actual Manager/settings/lock and emitter/writer over faithful native ports. Device selection is executed against a real-format synthetic proc block; no physical evdev reader, full Main process or compositor was exercised. Main forwarding is source-only. No already-reported absolute multitouch centroid/reset defect is re-counted.

findings.title: Published CapsWord menu changes leave the active session on its old policy
findings.reproduction: Before activation disable all six CapsWord pointer auto-off kinds so navigating/clicking the menu preserves the session. Activate CapsWord. Invoke the original Space checkbox callback: it persists unchecked and the settings policy no longer contains space, but the next typed space still ends/unlocks the session. In a separate session with left_click initially false, invoke the original left-click checkbox callback to enable it. The rebuilt original submenu is checked and the cached policy is true, yet the next native BTN_LEFT press leaves CapsWord active. After toggling off and activating a new session the same settings take effect. Idle0→1 and10→1 public setters show the same stale active snapshot.
findings.root_cause: modules.shortcuts.manager.start_caps_word stores the then-current CapsWordAutoOff.policy object in _caps_word_policy. caps_word_auto_off.persist publishes a new settings and policy object after an acknowledged write, but neither the menu callback nor active manager observers refresh _caps_word_policy or its scheduled idle chain. ui.menu.menu_shortcuts explicitly promises each change applies to the running CapsWord from its next event.
findings.silent_failure: The file write, cached settings, rebuilt checkboxes and menu-change notification all succeed, with no failure warning. Existing menu tests stop at saved bytes/rebuilt rows; existing session tests select policy before activation, so neither tests the publication-to-active-session transition.
findings.regression_test: Through original menu callbacks and actual active Manager/Hook, test enabling and disabling each terminator/pointer choice while CapsWord is active, including all-pointer-off preconditions needed to reach the menu. Assert the next event follows the acknowledged setting without restarting. Test idle0→positive, shorter/longer and positive→0 with exact timer custody and session-generation protection; retain conditional-write refusal and next-session controls.
findings.qualification: Executed original CapsWord submenu closure with actual shared renderer, real settings writer, active Manager and real Hook/lock/emitter/writer over controlled native ports. Only outer unrelated menu group rendering is intercepted; native tray clicks and a desktop application are not executed. External hand-edits being activation-scoped are distinct from the explicitly promised immediate menu path.
findings.root_adjudication: Confirmed written-live-apply-contract/runtime mismatch. The active snapshot is directly observed; shared product intent for setting lifetime is not inferred. Resolve the contradictory Linux menu promise versus snapshot ownership before choosing code changes or contract alignment. Windows explicitly documents next activation instead.

findings.title: Generic action output also omits the CapsWord checked-delimiter consumer
findings.reproduction: Before activation set CapsWord idle0, terminators=[enter] (then independently [tab]) and all six pointer auto-off kinds false. Activate CapsWord, persist primary_a=enter/tab through the actual keyboard binding owner, then deliver physical Ctrl+A through actual Hook and Keyboard.consume with admitted deferral. Real action catalogue/emitter/writer acknowledges exactly one KEY_ENTER28 or KEY_TAB15 DOWN/UP. CapsWord and capture CapsLock remain active; the following B capture is uppercase. Bare physical, literal-injector and ordinary KEY_TAPS controls end the checked session.
findings.root_cause: The existing WRSL-001 generic catalogue-output branch lacks canonical effect publication. Its already documented arrow/word/AI omission also leaves the independent CapsWord consumer uninformed for Enter/Tab. Main observes Hook semantics and literal injector output only; ComboEmitter has no CapsWord observer and own uinput is excluded from physical feedback.
findings.silent_failure: The real writer acknowledges the complete recorded key chord and the executor reports execution; no diagnostic names the absent CapsWord consumer. Successful emitter-order, physical-delimiter and literal-injector tests do not join generic catalogue output to this consumer.
findings.regression_test: Extend WRSL-001 regression/implementation to the CapsWord Enter/Tab consumer: real keyboard assignment, admitted queued delivery, checked/unchecked delimiters, ACK/refusal/partial output, next-key case and exact lifecycle/admission ownership. Preserve ordinary KEY_TAPS semantic relay and literal observer without double notifications; do not substitute WordReset/AI options for CapsWord delimiter settings.
findings.overlap_rationale: Same generic catalogue emission connector explicitly identified in prior WRSL-001 root(A); this is one newly demonstrated consumer and acceptance requirement, not a new independent architectural root or an ordinary tap Enter/Tab failure.
findings.qualification: Actual Lua owners, configuration and recorded native ACK boundary; no full Main closure or physical receiving application. Source-only Main forwarding and the existing root record are independently authenticated.

coverage.qualification: Actual feature model: all eight are settings. Supported macOS rows require Karabiner, Linux requires evdev/uinput, and Windows requires none. No native availability certification.
Both default and recommended are 10 s; presets are 0, 1, 3, 5, 10, 30, 60. A setting does not independently activate CapsWord. The actual menu has no free-entry command.
Actual shared corpus and extended zero control; AHK uses a zero sentinel rather than Lua nil.
Corpus covers before, at and after thresholds; extended 0.5 ms and 1 ms accepted values expire at 1 ms after quantization. Controlled numeric clocks only.
CW-S001: measured Lua policy outputs, source-only AHK comparison. Handwritten configuration edge; no shipped preset affected.
1e308 seconds is accepted and converted to positive infinity. Policy-only result; native timer admission and Windows arithmetic are unexecuted. No separate confirmed finding.
Shared-model default and recommended lists agree: space, nbsp, nnbsp, tab, enter, comma, semicolon, period.

Shared policy alone does not establish all driver timer scheduling.

Final A/B sweeps each run six processes, including both magic-key characterizations after CW-S002. No additional root was found in this bounded scope; repetitions do not add distinct coverage or certify native parity.

Local literal-versus-dynamic intent remains unresolved. Windows fresh literal catalogue is explicit, full caption not claimed.

findings.title: Accepted positive sub-millisecond idle delay becomes immediate expiry on Lua and disabled expiry in the AHK port
findings.qualification: Actual shared Lua 5.4/LuaJIT; Windows is source-only, with no AHK execution. The Linux reviewer corroborates actual Manager admission through controlled native ports, not native desktop elapsed-time measurement. macOS public timer receiving remains owned by its reviewer. This requires a hand-edited or programmatic positive delay below 0.0005 s; shipped menu presets and the 10 s defaults are unaffected.
findings.reproduction: Set shortcuts.caps_word.idle_timeout_seconds = 0.0001 with valid terminators and pointer settings; activate CapsWord. The shared validator accepts this positive number. Both ports round 0.1 ms to zero. Lua keeps numeric zero and represents disabled only by nil, so idle_expired(policy, 100, 100) is true. The AHK port represents disabled by zero and requires idle_ms > 0 before expiry, so this rounded positive value disables automatic expiry there. Controls: seconds = 0 disables; seconds = 0.0005 and 0.001 become 1 ms and expire at the 1 ms boundary. The Linux reviewer records actual Manager queueing a 0 ms check on activation, with the recorded scheduler ending the session when that due callback runs.
findings.root_cause: Millisecond quantization is not validated against the disabled sentinel. Lua and AHK assign different meanings to the rounded numeric zero produced from an accepted positive setting.
findings.silent_failure: The ordinary menu only offers whole-second presets. The existing shared corpus covers zero, positive whole seconds, and 2.5 s, but no value whose millisecond representation rounds to zero. It therefore misses the representation collision.
findings.regression_test: Extend the handwritten shared corpus with 0, 0.0001, 0.00049, 0.0005 and 0.001; define one cross-driver rejection or minimum-positive quantization rule and replay both actual policy ports. Include public timer admission controls: disabled zero creates no expiry, while every accepted positive value has an enabled positive delay. Preserve whole-second presets, 2.5 s and exact thresholds. Windows AHK execution and native timer receiving remain required.

findings.title: CapsWord delimiter menus display the renamed magic key while the active policy still reads the literal star
findings.qualification: Actual shared Lua mutation/load controls; actual macOS/Linux public menu/event corroboration is retained by the OS reviewers and independently replayed by the root. Windows documents a separate fresh built-in catalogue; its full translated caption has not been established here. No physical native key receiving is claimed.
findings.reproduction: With the ordinary shared policy already loaded, choose the valid magic key § through the driver owner, choose only the built-in star CapsWord delimiter, disable other auto-off causes for isolation, and activate CapsWord. The macOS/Linux menu substitutes § in the checked delimiter caption. The actual active rule still matches literal ★: § leaves CapsWord active while ★ ends it. In shared Lua, loading the policy after a real Terminators.update_magic_key("§") reverses the captured scalar, which characterizes load-order sensitivity rather than universal boot behavior.
findings.root_cause: The menu substitutes the current hotstring magic key in a stable built-in CapsWord slot label, but the CapsWord policy reads a separately captured catalogue. On macOS, replacing the star definition chars table leaves the policy module holding the previous table. On Linux, the production magic-key owners update their own metadata without a production Terminators.update_magic_key caller, so the actual CapsWord rule remains literal. Windows explicitly documents a fresh built-in catalogue separate from hotstring renaming; the intended cross-driver literal-versus-dynamic policy is not settled.
findings.silent_failure: The shared star corpus and default menus use the shipped ★ glyph, where menu and policy agree. Existing tests do not jointly change the public magic key, draw the actual CapsWord delimiter checkbox and deliver both old and new scalars through its active owner. A source check for label substitution alone would certify the misleading caption.
findings.regression_test: Decide whether CapsWord star means the literal built-in scalar or the current magic key, then make the actual policy and its menu label agree. Test a public rename to § with an already-loaded policy and with fresh startup order, draw the actual menu, activate the actual mode and deliver both scalars under the single selected slot. Cover macOS replacement-table capture and Linux metadata ownership independently. Do not prescribe dynamic renaming merely because the menu currently substitutes it; preserve an explicitly chosen literal policy if that is the product decision.
